comment: Jim is hilarious and a chill guy. The class itself is not too hard; just be prepared to study up for the exams. The problem sets in R can be a pain though. Take him!

His way of teaching is quite boring and the assignments every week do not  reflect at all what you do in class. His exams have nothing really to do with his assignments and in generell I feel like I haven't really learned a whole lot in this course!

Had him for ECON 370 Advanced Econometrics. Dr Monks is the man. Smart funny guy. Lectures make a lot of sense, answers our questions well. Problem sets use R, but he posts example code for similar questions so you can get by even with no R experience. Not really any curveballs, sets clear expectations on what to know for quizzes/midterm.

Lots of lectures in class. These can be helpful as I never had to read the textbook, but he goes a little fast and can be hard to follow. You have to memorize complex formulas for tests and quizzes, which can be overwhelming. Make sure to work hard on HW, as it is similar to tests and quizzes and doing well on HW can bump your grade up.

The way the class is set up is just terrible. He does the problems in class on paper, doesn't post any notes, the homework's are in excel, yet the tests are on paper! DO not take him unless you want a horrible class experience.

Professor Monks is one of the best professors I have had. Be ready to pay attention and take good notes and the class will be manageable. The one con is that tests are 90% of the grade. Other than that he is a very respectable guy that wants you to succeed.

He lectures most of the class, not many chances to participate but easy to ask questions. He does an example or two then we have weekly problem sets. Basically exactly what we did in class but with data sets or by hand. Other than the problem sets nothing else is due. Quizzes are 1-2 questions from the PS. Exams are PS/quizzes just longer.

Dr. Monks is such a great professor. Aside from being hilarious, he gives really good lectures and goes through examples in class that you see on the homework and tests. Quizzes are easy and exams are a direct reflection of class, homework, and quizzes. He really cares about his students doing well and is always willing to help outside of class

Dr. Monks is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is smart, funny, and is enthusiastic about what he teaches. ECON 271 is tough with any professor so don't be scared away by him being a challenging instructor. Really good guy and a great professor.

A horrible professor who is smug and does not offer much additional help to students outside of class. You are required to memorize an absurd amount of formulas for the exam and the homework is on R Studio and has no correlation with the exams.

Was whack. In class we did all theoretical problems with bstats, in the homeworks it was all excel problems and then for our assesments it was all probelms that we had to write down! nothing we did in class carried over to our tests, just not a smoothly run class

I wouldn't consider Jim Monks to even be a professor as I viewed him more as a father during my semester with him. A tough loving father that wanted to see you be the man he once envisioned himself to become. Do the problem sets, meet with him if you have questions and you'll be chillin.

Terrible professor, obviously very knowledgeable, but does a poor job at putting things in terms where students can understand. Lectures at you and requires you to remember many formulas for exams. Not very helpful outside of class.

Lectures at you, rather than engages with you, which doesnt work well for bstats. Just weites stuff on the board and youre expected to copy and memorize all the formulas. Hard teacher if youve never taken a statistics class before or arent used to memorizing formulas.
Amazing professor. Very enthusiastic and involved. The course is also interesting if you like learning and problem sets are well constructed
Wont stop moving around during class but its entertaining. Especially when he starts ranting about whatever we distract him with.
Monk is a tough, but fair teacher who wants his students to do well.  Lectures are interesting and if you study you should do alright.

Have fun teaching yourself all of the material.  His lectures are confusing and poorly planned out.  He makes you memorize an absurd amount of equations for the tests.  If you ever meet with him outside of class, expect for him to be sarcastic and rude.

He is one of the easiest econ professor at UR. I would strongly recommend him. His exams are almost identical to his quizzes. The only thing I don't like about his class is that he does not give A+. He makes people econ majors!!!

Prof. Monks is the best!! He is a must take in the econ department. He is hilarious, has great way of putting things into contexts and examples that you remember and understand concepts and enjoys answering challenging questions. He is the most helpful office hours professor. He spent hours explaining the simplest concepts!

I wholeheartedly declare that Monks is the best teacher I have ever had. He is an extremely effective teacher--he presents information clearly and consistently in an understandable manner, and he understands/listens to students questions well. He is entertaining and funny, and students feel comfortable around him.

Not an easy class. There is a ton of material covered and a lot of formulas to memorize. Don't expect a cheat sheet. Some of the material he explains well when he's just writing on the board but the excel stuff was really confusing. Problem sets are tough, quizes and tests aren't bad but you have to study hard!

On tests, you have to use one of the bschool calculators to run functions usually reserved for Excel. That explains a lot. Granted they're not terrible to learn, THIS IS BY NO MEANS AN EASY CLASS. DON'T EXPECT AN A.

Monks is a great teacher.  Weekly homework is not graded and doesn't take too long.  Very helpful during office hours.  Tests are tough (but nothing unpredictable shows up, especially if you spend time figuring out the homework).  He's very good about giving partial credit on quizzes/tests.  Also a pretty entertaining guy in class as well.

Monks is by no means easy.  If you can take the other professors, I would, but Monks was still great.  He is funny and entertaining as he knows the class is boring.  If you study, and work, you can do well as Monks wants you to do well (but no curves ever). Not a great class, but a great professor.

Monks makes class interesting by using current data from students at UR. He doesn't give a huge research paper anymore and his homework is not actually graded, and only given once a week. His tests are not hard, the final is not cumulative and there are 5 or so 10 point quizzes and drops the lowest.
Dr. Monks is by no means an easy A, but he's an excellent professor who knows his stuff.  You pretty much just can't be lazy, or you'll do poorly.  Helpful outside of class too.

Taking Monks was the biggest mistake of my college career.  On a personal level, he is a nice guy, but his demands from students are outrageous and he has lost sight of the fact that people being exposed to (for ex.) multiple regressions for the 1st time might have some trouble grasping their conceptual framework.
Boring Class. Decent teacher. Boring class, granted the material he teaches isnt mind blowing. Assigns a 10 page research paper.
No Comments

Monks is a smart guy who gives good lectures and makes you interested in the material. However, he is not very friendly and won't go out of his way to help you. You have to participate and show interest if you want to be on his good side. He definitely has favorites. I managed an A in the class b/c I did these things.

If your looking for an easy A, this is not the course, but two years after graduation, working in a field that does not require this stuff, I still remember how to run an anova, and was the only one in the office who could explain a t test. Any professor t
stay away
